name: Almond Butter Chia Pudding
steps: Whisk the chia seeds into the almond milk with the maple syrup.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours, or overnight, stirring once.
Once set, swirl through the almond butter.
Top with raspberries before serving.
meal_prep_tip: Like overnight oats, built to make ahead — a batch keeps for up to 5 days in the fridge.

name: Apple with Peanut Butter
steps: Slice the apple.
Serve with the peanut butter for dipping.
meal_prep_tip: About as simple as it gets — there's not much to prep beyond portioning the peanut butter.

name: Baked Salmon with Quinoa
steps: Cook the quinoa according to packet instructions.
Place the salmon and asparagus on a tray, drizzle with olive oil and season.
Bake at 200°C for 12-15 minutes until the salmon is just cooked through.
Serve over the quinoa with a squeeze of lemon.
meal_prep_tip: The quinoa keeps for 4 days; salmon is best baked fresh but only takes 12-15 minutes, so this is easy to half-prep.

name: Banana Honey Milk Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until smooth and frothy.
Serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Best blended fresh. Freeze the banana ahead for an even thicker, colder shake.

name: Bean & Sausage Hotpot
steps: Brown the sausages whole in a dry pan over a medium heat for 6 minutes, turning, then lift out and slice into 2cm rounds.
Soften the onion and carrot in the same pan for 6-8 minutes until the onion is translucent and starting to colour.
Return the sausages, add the chopped tomatoes, and simmer for 10 minutes to reduce and concentrate.
Stir in the baked beans and warm through for 5 minutes. Do not boil hard once the beans are in or they break up.
Season and check the sausages are cooked through before serving.
meal_prep_tip: Better the next day once the flavours settle. Keeps for 3 days and freezes for 2 months.

name: Beef & Egg Breakfast Hash
steps: Dice the potato into 1.5cm cubes and parboil for 6 minutes, then drain well and leave to steam dry for 2 minutes. Dry potato is what crisps.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the potato for 8-10 minutes without stirring too often, until a crust forms.
Push the potato to one side, add the onion and beef mince, and brown for 5 minutes, breaking the mince up as it cooks until no pink remains.
Stir everything together, season well, and press flat. Leave for 2 minutes to catch on the base.
Make a well in the middle, crack in the egg, cover the pan and cook for 3 minutes until the white is set.
meal_prep_tip: The hash keeps for 3 days and reheats well in a hot pan. Cook the egg fresh each time — reheated egg turns rubbery.

name: Beef Burrito Bowl
steps: Brown the beef mince in a hot pan with your preferred taco seasoning.
Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Warm the black beans and sweetcorn.
Layer rice, beef, beans and sweetcorn in a bowl, topped with salsa.
meal_prep_tip: All the components keep for 4 days — cook once, portion into containers, and you're set for the week.

name: Beef Chilli Con Carne
steps: Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef mince and break it up with a spoon, cooking for 5-6 minutes until browned all over.
Add the chilli (start with less — you can always add more) and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the drained kidney beans and the tinned tomatoes, plus half a tin of water. Season with salt and pepper.

Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low and cook uncovered for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened and rich. Mash a few beans against the side of the pan to thicken it further.
About 12 minutes before serving, cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Taste and adjust the chilli and salt, then serve over the rice. Freezes extremely well — a double batch is worth it.
meal_prep_tip: Freezes and reheats excellently — a genuine batch-cook staple.

name: Beef Jerky & Apple
steps: Slice the apple.
Serve alongside the beef jerky.
Eat together for a sweet-savoury, high-protein snack.
meal_prep_tip: Nothing to really prep — jerky keeps on its own and apples are best sliced fresh.

name: Beef Stir Fry
steps: Cook the noodles according to packet instructions and set aside.
Sear the beef strips in a very hot wok or pan for 1-2 minutes, then remove.
Stir-fry the broccoli and pepper for 3-4 minutes until just tender.
Return the beef to the pan, add the noodles and soy sauce, and toss together until hot.
meal_prep_tip: Stir-fries are best cooked fresh since the vegetables lose their crunch on reheating, but you can marinate the beef up to a day ahead.

name: Berry & Oat Smoothie
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until completely smooth — the oats thicken it up.
Serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Keep frozen berries and pre-portioned oats ready — this blends in under a minute.

name: Bircher Muesli
steps: Coarsely grate the whole apple, skin on, straight into a bowl or jar — discard the core.
Add the oats, Greek yogurt, milk and cinnamon to the grated apple.
Stir thoroughly until everything is evenly combined and no dry oats remain.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight — the oats need time to soften and absorb the liquid.
Before eating, stir again and loosen with a splash more milk if it's thicker than you like. Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.
meal_prep_tip: Same idea as overnight oats — make a batch on Sunday, keeps well for 4-5 days.

name: Boiled Eggs & Nuts
steps: Boil the eggs for 8-10 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Portion the almonds and walnuts alongside.
Season the eggs with a little salt and pepper if you like.
meal_prep_tip: Boil a batch of 6-8 eggs at once — they keep in the shell in the fridge for a week.

name: Breakfast Burrito
steps: Warm the black beans in a small pan over low heat for 3-4 minutes, or microwave for 60-90 seconds. Season with a pinch of salt and cumin if you have it.

Whisk 3 eggs with a pinch of salt. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat with a little oil or butter, pour in the eggs, and scramble gently with a spatula for 2-3 minutes, pulling the eggs from the edges to the centre. Take them off the heat while still slightly soft — they'll finish cooking in the wrap.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20-30 seconds per side, or 15 seconds in the microwave, so it's flexible and won't crack.
Lay the tortilla flat. Spoon the scrambled eggs down the centre in a line, leaving 5cm clear at each end. Top with the black beans, grated cheddar and salsa.
Fold the two short ends inwards, then roll tightly away from you, keeping the filling tucked in. For a sealed finish, place the burrito seam-side down in the hot pan for 1 minute.
Slice in half diagonally and serve.
meal_prep_tip: Assemble a batch, wrap individually in foil, and freeze — reheat from frozen in the microwave.

name: Bulking Beef & Pasta Bake
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the pasta in salted boiling water for 2 minutes LESS than the packet says — it finishes cooking in the oven.
While the pasta cooks, heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Brown the beef mince for 5-6 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the passata, season with salt, pepper and any herbs you like (oregano works well), and simmer for 10 minutes.
Drain the pasta and stir it through the sauce until fully coated. Transfer everything to an ovenproof dish.
Top with the grated cheddar and bake for 15 minutes until the cheese is melted, bubbling and golden in spots.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving. Around 1550 kcal as a whole — it comfortably splits into two portions if that's over your target, and reheats well for 4 days.
meal_prep_tip: Make a double batch and portion into containers — reheats well for up to 4 days.

name: Bulking Peanut Butter Oats
steps: Combine the oats and plant milk in a saucepan over medium heat.
Cook for 5-6 minutes, stirring regularly, until thick and creamy — add a splash more milk if it gets too stiff.
Take off the heat and stir in the peanut butter until fully melted through.
Transfer to a bowl and top with the sliced banana, a drizzle of honey and the chia seeds.
For a no-cook version: mix everything cold in a jar the night before and refrigerate — it's ready by morning.
This makes one very large portion (~1080 kcal). Halve everything for a standard breakfast.
meal_prep_tip: Make overnight: combine everything cold, refrigerate overnight, eat in the morning. Great for bulking phases.

name: Chicken & Halloumi Burger
steps: Butterfly the chicken breast by slicing it horizontally almost in half and opening it out, then bash it to an even thickness. It cooks in half the time and stays juicy.
Season and griddle over a medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes each side, until the juices run clear and there is no pink at the thickest point.
Dry-fry the halloumi for 2 minutes each side until golden. No oil needed.
Toast the cut sides of the bun in the same pan for 30 seconds.
Build: mayo, lettuce, chicken, halloumi, tomato. Serve straight away while the halloumi is still soft.
meal_prep_tip: Cook the chicken ahead if you like, but the halloumi has to be fresh — it sets firm within minutes of leaving the pan.

name: Chicken Caesar Wrap
steps: If your chicken isn't already cooked: season a 150g chicken breast with salt and pepper and pan-fry over medium heat for 6-7 minutes per side until the internal temperature reaches 74°C (or the juices run clear when pierced). Rest for 3 minutes, then slice.
Roughly chop the romaine lettuce and add to a bowl with the sliced chicken and shaved parmesan.
Add the caesar dressing and toss until everything is lightly coated.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20-30 seconds per side so it's flexible.
Pile the filling down the centre of the wrap, fold in the short ends, and roll tightly.
Slice in half diagonally and serve, or wrap in foil to take with you.
meal_prep_tip: Best assembled fresh so the wrap doesn't go soggy, but the chicken can be cooked and sliced up to 3 days ahead.

name: Chicken Fajitas
steps: Toss the sliced chicken with the fajita seasoning.
Stir-fry the chicken in a hot pan for 5-6 minutes until nearly cooked.
Add the peppers and onion, cooking for a further 4-5 minutes until softened.
Warm the tortillas and serve everything together to build your own fajitas.
meal_prep_tip: Cook the chicken and peppers in bulk and reheat — keeps well for 3-4 days, just warm the tortillas fresh.

name: Chicken Katsu Curry
steps: Coat the chicken breast in flour, egg and panko, then shallow-fry until golden and cooked through.
Simmer the carrot in the curry sauce until soft, about 10-12 minutes.
Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Slice the chicken and serve over rice with the curry sauce poured over.
meal_prep_tip: The panko coating goes soft if stored assembled — prep the sauce and rice ahead, but fry the chicken fresh, or re-crisp it in the oven.

name: Chicken Pesto Pasta
steps: Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water according to packet instructions until al dente. Before draining, save a small cup of the pasta water.
While the pasta cooks, season the chicken breast and pan-fry over medium heat for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through (internal temp 74°C, or juices run clear). Rest for 3 minutes, then slice.
Drain the pasta and return it to the pan off the heat. Add the pesto and a splash of the reserved pasta water, and toss — the starchy water helps the pesto coat every piece.
Stir through the halved cherry tomatoes.
Top with the sliced chicken and a scattering of parmesan. Serve hot or cold — it works well as a packed lunch the next day.
meal_prep_tip: Keeps well cold or reheated for 3-4 days — a solid make-ahead lunch.

name: Chicken Sausage & Egg Wrap
steps: Grill or pan-fry the chicken sausages until cooked through, then slice.
Scramble the eggs in a separate pan.
Warm the tortilla, then layer spinach, egg and sausage down the centre.
Add hot sauce, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
meal_prep_tip: Best assembled fresh, but you can cook the sausage and scramble the eggs up to 3 days ahead and just reheat and wrap each morning.

name: Chicken Shawarma Bowl
steps: Season the chicken thigh with paprika and grill or pan-fry until cooked through, then slice.
Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Build the bowl with rice as the base, topped with chicken and diced cucumber.
Finish with a generous spoon of garlic sauce.
meal_prep_tip: Cook the chicken and rice in bulk, keep the cucumber and garlic sauce separate, and combine fresh — the base keeps for 4 days.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
steps: Cut the chicken breast into 3cm cubes and season with salt and half the garam masala.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned on the outside and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, pour in the passata and the remaining garam masala, scraping up any browned bits from the base — that's flavour. Simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the cream, then return the chicken to the sauce and warm through for 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning, then serve over the rice. Like most curries, this tastes even better reheated the next day.
meal_prep_tip: Keeps and reheats well for 3-4 days, and the flavour deepens overnight.

name: Chilli Prawn Linguine
steps: Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil and cook the linguine for 9-10 minutes, until just tender with a slight bite. Reserve a mugful of the cooking water before draining.

While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a frying pan over a low heat and soften the sliced garlic and chilli for 2 minutes. Keep the heat low so the garlic turns pale gold rather than brown, which would make it bitter.
Raise the heat to medium and add the prawns. Cook for 2-3 minutes, turning once, until they have turned pink all over and curled into a loose C shape. Tightly curled prawns are overcooked.
Add the drained linguine to the pan with a splash of the reserved pasta water and toss for 30 seconds, until the starchy water loosens into a light sauce that coats the strands.
Season, and serve straight away while the prawns are still tender.
meal_prep_tip: Best eaten fresh, as reheated prawns turn rubbery. For a head start, slice the garlic and chilli and cook the linguine in advance, then rinse, toss in a little oil and chill. The sauce takes 5 minutes from cold.

name: Chocolate Peanut Butter Protein Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Pour and drink immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Pre-portion the protein powder and cocoa into bags — just add milk, banana and peanut butter and blend when ready.

name: Cod & Sweet Potato Traybake
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cube the sweet potato into 2cm chunks.
Toss the sweet potato with half the olive oil, salt and pepper on a large baking tray, spread in a single layer, and roast for 20 minutes.
Add the broccoli florets and whole garlic cloves to the tray, toss with the remaining oil, and roast for a further 10 minutes.

Push the vegetables to the sides, place the cod fillet in the centre, season it, and return the tray to the oven for 10-12 minutes. The cod is done when it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork — don't overcook it or it turns rubbery.
Squeeze the softened roasted garlic out of its skins over the fish, add a squeeze of lemon if you have one, and serve straight from the tray.
meal_prep_tip: Best roasted fresh so the fish doesn't overcook on reheating, but the sweet potato and broccoli can be chopped up to 2 days ahead.

name: Coffee Protein Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Good as a pre-workout or breakfast-on-the-go option.
meal_prep_tip: Batch-brew cold coffee at the start of the week and keep it in the fridge — the rest blends together in seconds.

name: Cottage Cheese & Berries
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl.
Top with blueberries.
Drizzle with honey and serve.
meal_prep_tip: Keep the cottage cheese and berries separate in the fridge and combine when you want it — both keep for a week.

name: Cottage Cheese Pancakes
steps: Add the cottage cheese, eggs, oats and banana to a blender. Blend for 30-45 seconds until mostly smooth — a little texture from the oats is fine.
Let the batter rest for 5 minutes; it will thicken slightly as the oats absorb moisture.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and add a small amount of oil or butter, wiping out any excess with kitchen paper.
Pour small rounds of batter (about 3 tablespoons each) into the pan — don't overcrowd, cook 2-3 at a time.

Cook for about 2 minutes until bubbles appear on the surface and the underside is golden, then flip carefully and cook another 1-2 minutes. The pancakes are done when they spring back lightly when pressed.
Keep warm under foil while you cook the rest. Serve warm with fruit.
meal_prep_tip: Freezes well between sheets of baking paper — reheat in a toaster.

name: Cottage Pie
steps: Boil the potato in salted water for 18-20 minutes until a knife slides in with no resistance, then drain and steam dry for 2 minutes before mashing.
Brown the mince in a dry pan over a high heat for 5 minutes without stirring much — you want colour, which is where the flavour comes from.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 8 minutes until softened, then pour in the stock and simmer for 15 minutes until thickened.
Season the mash generously and spread it over the mince in an ovenproof dish, roughing the top with a fork so it catches.
Bake at 200C / 180C fan for 20-25 minutes until the top is golden and the edges are bubbling.
meal_prep_tip: Assemble a day ahead and bake straight from the fridge with an extra 10 minutes. Freezes for 3 months, cooked or uncooked.

name: Edamame with Sea Salt
steps: Steam or boil the edamame for 4-5 minutes until tender.
Drain and toss with sea salt.
Squeeze over a little lime before serving.
meal_prep_tip: Cook a big batch and keep in the fridge for 3-4 days, or freeze pre-cooked portions.

name: Egg Fried Rice with Prawns
steps: Cook the rice according to packet instructions, spread it on a plate, and let it cool completely — or better, use cold rice cooked the day before. Cold, dry rice fries properly; warm fresh rice turns mushy.
Heat a wok or large frying pan over high heat until smoking, then add a tablespoon of oil.
Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble quickly for 30-45 seconds until just set. Remove and set aside.
Add the prawns to the hot pan and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until pink and cooked through. Add the peas for the final minute.
Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps with your spatula, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until every grain is hot and starting to catch slightly.
Return the egg to the pan, add the soy sauce, and toss everything together for a final 30 seconds. Serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Reheats well, and day-old rice actually works better for this than fresh — great with leftover rice.

name: Falafel Salad
steps: Shape and bake or pan-fry the falafel until golden and crisp on the outside.
Toss the mixed leaves, tomato and cucumber together as a base.
Top the salad with the warm falafel.
Drizzle with tahini dressing to finish.
meal_prep_tip: Bake a big batch of falafel — they reheat well — and keep the dressing separate until you're ready to eat.

name: Full English Breakfast
steps: Grill the bacon and sausages until cooked through.
Fry the mushrooms in the same pan for a few minutes.
Warm the baked beans in a small pan.
Fry or poach the eggs and plate everything together.
meal_prep_tip: A fresh-cook — eggs and bacon don't reheat well together — though you can pre-chop the mushrooms the night before.

name: Greek Yogurt Protein Bowl
steps: Spoon the Greek yogurt into a bowl.
Scatter the mixed berries over the top.
Sprinkle on the granola and chia seeds.
Finish with a drizzle of honey and serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Portion yogurt and berries into containers for up to 4 days; keep the granola separate and add it just before eating so it stays crunchy.

name: Greek Yogurt Protein Dip with Fruit
steps: Whisk the whey protein into the Greek yogurt until smooth.
Spoon into a bowl.
Top with chopped mixed fruit and a pinch of cinnamon.
Serve as a dip with the fruit, or eat straight with a spoon.
meal_prep_tip: The yogurt dip keeps for 3-4 days — just chop fresh fruit to go with it.

name: Green Protein Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Freeze pre-washed spinach and kale in portioned bags — wilted greens blend just as well as fresh.

name: Grilled Lamb Chops with Veg
steps: Marinate the lamb chops in olive oil, garlic and rosemary for at least 20 minutes.
Griddle or grill the chops for 3-4 minutes per side depending on thickness.
Grill or pan-fry the courgette slices alongside until charred and tender.
Rest the lamb for a few minutes before serving with the courgette.
meal_prep_tip: Best grilled fresh for texture, but you can marinate the lamb up to 24 hours ahead so it's ready to cook.

name: Halloumi & Roast Veg Salad
steps: Roast the courgette, red pepper and red onion at 200°C for 20 minutes.
Slice the halloumi and griddle or pan-fry until golden on both sides.
Toss the mixed leaves with the roasted vegetables.
Top with the warm halloumi and serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: The roasted veg keeps for 4 days; halloumi is best pan-fried fresh since it firms up once cold, but it only takes 3 minutes.

name: Halloumi & Tomato Breakfast Plate
steps: Slice the halloumi into 1cm slabs and pat them dry — wet halloumi steams instead of browning.
Dry-fry the halloumi over a medium-high heat for 2 minutes each side, until deep golden and squeaky. It needs no oil.
Halve the tomatoes and add them to the pan for the last 2 minutes, cut side down, until they blister and soften.
Fry the eggs in the same pan for 2-3 minutes, spooning the hot fat over the whites until set but the yolk still moves.
Pile onto a plate with the rocket and season. Halloumi is already salty, so taste before adding more.
meal_prep_tip: Halloumi is best cooked to order — it goes rubbery once cold. Slice it in advance and keep it in the fridge so the cooking takes three minutes.

name: High-Calorie Salmon & Rice
steps: Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Place the salmon on a lined baking tray, rub with half the olive oil, and season with salt and pepper.
Bake the salmon for 12-14 minutes, until it flakes easily at the thickest part.
Halve, stone and slice the avocado.
Plate the rice, place the salmon on top, arrange the avocado alongside, and finish with the remaining olive oil, a squeeze of lemon, and a pinch of salt.
At roughly 1500 kcal this is a serious bulking meal — the portion scaler will trim it to your target if needed.
meal_prep_tip: Best with freshly cooked salmon. The rice can be batch-cooked ahead — reheat with a splash of water.

name: Homemade Protein Bar
steps: Warm the honey and peanut butter together until runny.
Stir in the oats and protein powder until a thick dough forms.
Press into a small lined tray or tin.
Chill for at least 1 hour, then slice into bars.
Macros shown are per bar — the tray makes 4 bars.
meal_prep_tip: Keeps in the fridge for a week or freezes well — make a full tray at once.

name: Hummus & Veggie Sticks
steps: Spoon the hummus into a small bowl.
Arrange the carrot, cucumber and celery sticks around it.
Dip and eat.
meal_prep_tip: Chop a batch of veggie sticks and store with a damp paper towel to keep them crisp for up to 5 days.

name: Jacket Potato with Beans & Cheese
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Wash the potato, dry it, and prick it all over with a fork — this stops it bursting.

Rub the skin with a little oil and salt for a crispier finish, then bake directly on the oven shelf for 60-75 minutes, until a knife slides into the centre with no resistance. (Short on time? Microwave on high for 8-10 minutes, then crisp in the oven for 10 minutes at 220°C.)
About 5 minutes before the potato is done, warm the baked beans in a small pan over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Cut a deep cross into the top of the potato and squeeze the sides to open it up. Fluff the inside with a fork and season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the hot beans over the potato and top with the grated cheddar so it melts into the beans. Serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Bake a batch of potatoes and reheat one at a time — the beans keep too, so this comes together in minutes.

name: King Prawn Pad Thai
steps: Soak the rice noodles in just-boiled water for 8 minutes until pliable but still firm. They finish cooking in the pan and turn to paste if boiled.
Get a wok very hot. Fry the prawns for 2 minutes, turning once, until pink and curled into a loose C. Tightly curled means overcooked. Set aside.
Crack the egg into the empty wok and scramble it hard for 30 seconds.
Add the drained noodles and pad thai sauce and toss constantly for 2 minutes, until the noodles have absorbed the sauce and loosened.
Return the prawns, toss for 30 seconds, and serve scattered with crushed peanuts and a wedge of lime.
meal_prep_tip: Not a make-ahead dish — reheated rice noodles go gluey and reheated prawns go rubbery. Prep everything first and it cooks in five minutes.

name: Lamb & Lemon Souvlaki
steps: Cube the lamb into even 3cm pieces and toss with the juice of half the lemon, salt and pepper. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight.
Thread onto skewers, leaving small gaps so the heat reaches all sides.
Grill or griddle over a high heat for 8-10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until charred outside and just pink in the middle.
Rest the skewers for 5 minutes — lamb carries on cooking and the juices redistribute.
Serve with the yogurt, tomatoes and cucumber alongside.
meal_prep_tip: Marinate and skewer the day before. The lamb is better for the longer marinade, and it goes from fridge to plate in ten minutes.

name: Lamb Kofta Pitta
steps: Grate half the onion into the lamb mince, season heavily, and work it with your hands for a full minute — that stickiness is what stops kofta falling apart.
Shape into two sausages around 2cm thick. Chill for 10 minutes if you have time.
Grill or dry-fry over a medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until well browned and cooked through with no pink in the middle.
Slice the cucumber and remaining onion. Warm the pitta for 30 seconds and split it open.
Stuff with the kofta and salad, and spoon the yogurt over.
meal_prep_tip: The raw mixture keeps for a day and freezes for a month once shaped. Cook from frozen with an extra 4 minutes.

name: Lentil Dahl with Rice
steps: Rinse the lentils, then simmer with turmeric and garlic in water until soft, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer a further 5 minutes until creamy.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Serve the dahl over the rice.
meal_prep_tip: Freezes exceptionally well — make a double batch and freeze half in portions for a genuinely ready meal later.

name: Mango & Coconut Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Serve cold.
meal_prep_tip: Freeze mango chunks ahead — they keep for months and make the shake thicker without ice.

name: Mass Builder Chicken Rice Bowl
steps: Cook the rice according to packet instructions — 150g dry rice needs about 300ml of water and 12-15 minutes.
Butterfly the chicken breasts (slice horizontally almost all the way through and open like a book) so they cook evenly. Season well with salt and pepper.

Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 5-6 minutes per side until golden and cooked through (internal temp 74°C, juices run clear). Rest for 3 minutes, then slice.
Halve, stone and dice the avocado.
Layer the rice in a large bowl, top with the sliced chicken and avocado, and drizzle with soy sauce.
This is a genuinely big meal at around 1500 kcal — if that's more than your target, the portion scaler will size it down, or split it into two meals.
meal_prep_tip: Cook a double or triple batch of rice and chicken on Sunday — this is one of the best batch-cook bulking meals.

name: Mass Gainer Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until smooth — this one's thick, so add a splash more milk if needed.
Sip rather than gulp if you're not used to the volume.
meal_prep_tip: Batch-measure the oats and protein powder into containers for the week — worth having a routine for if you're bulking.

name: Massive Chicken Wrap
steps: Season the chicken breast and pan-fry over medium heat for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through (74°C internal, juices run clear). Rest 3 minutes, then slice into strips.
Warm both tortillas in a dry pan for 20-30 seconds per side so they're flexible.
Halve, stone and slice the avocado.
Divide the chicken, avocado, grated cheddar and Greek yogurt between the two wraps, keeping the filling in a line down the centre with space at the ends.
Fold in the ends and roll each wrap tightly. For a toasted finish, return each wrap seam-side down to the hot pan for 1 minute.
Around 1330 kcal for both wraps — eat one now and save the second (they keep a day wrapped in foil), or have both if you're deep in a bulk.
meal_prep_tip: Cook the chicken in bulk ahead — just slice and assemble fresh each day. Avocado is best added fresh.

name: Mediterranean Couscous Salad
steps: Put the couscous in a heatproof bowl and pour over 100ml of boiling water or hot vegetable stock (just enough to cover it by a few millimetres). Cover the bowl with a plate and leave for 5 minutes.
Uncover and fluff the couscous thoroughly with a fork to separate the grains.
Stir through the drained chickpeas and diced cucumber.
Top with the crumbled feta and olives.
Dress with a tablespoon of olive oil, a squeeze of lemon juice, salt and pepper. Toss gently and serve. Keeps in the fridge for 3-4 days — the flavour actually improves after a few hours.
meal_prep_tip: Keeps well for 3-4 days — actually improves after a day as the flavours settle.

name: Mushroom & Spinach Frittata
steps: Slice the mushrooms and fry in the oil over a high heat for 6-8 minutes. Do not crowd or salt them early or they will stew instead of browning.
Add the spinach and toss until wilted, about 1 minute, then tip out any liquid — wet filling makes a soggy frittata.
Beat the eggs with plenty of seasoning and most of the cheese.
Return the vegetables to the pan, spread them out, and pour the egg over. Cook on a low heat for 8-10 minutes until the edges are set and only the centre wobbles.
Scatter the remaining cheese and finish under a hot grill for 2-3 minutes until puffed and golden.
meal_prep_tip: One of the best cold lunches there is. Keeps 3 days in the fridge and does not need reheating.

name: Overnight Oats with Peanut Butter
steps: Combine the oats, plant milk, chia seeds and a tablespoon of peanut butter in a jar.
Stir well, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning top with sliced banana and the remaining peanut butter.
Stir and eat cold, or warm briefly if preferred.
meal_prep_tip: Built for exactly this — make up to 4 jars on Sunday, they keep well for 4-5 days in the fridge.

name: Paneer Tikka Masala
steps: Lightly fry the paneer cubes until golden on the edges, then set aside.
Simmer the passata with garam masala for 10 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the cream and return the paneer to the sauce, warming through.
Serve over cooked basmati rice.
meal_prep_tip: Curries like this genuinely improve after a day in the fridge — one of the better make-ahead dinners here.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Protein Toast
ingredients: 0.5 scoop, stirred into the peanut butter
steps: Toast the 2 slices of wholemeal bread to your preferred level.

In a small bowl, mix the whey protein into the peanut butter, adding water half a teaspoon at a time (roughly 2-3 teaspoons total) until it loosens to a spreadable consistency. It will seize up at first — keep stirring.
Spread the protein-peanut butter mix evenly over both slices of toast.
Top with banana slices and eat immediately while the toast is warm.
meal_prep_tip: Best assembled fresh so the toast stays crisp, though the peanut butter mix can be made in one batch.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Freeze the banana ahead for a thicker shake. The peanut butter and oat milk keep on the shelf.

name: Poached Egg & Watercress on Toast
steps: Bring a pan of water to a bare simmer. A splash of vinegar helps the whites hold together but is not essential with fresh eggs.
Crack each egg into a cup and slide it into the water. Poach for 3 minutes for a soft yolk, 4 for firmer.
Toast and butter the bread while the eggs cook.
Halve the tomatoes and scatter them with the watercress over the toast.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon, drain on kitchen paper for a few seconds so the toast stays crisp, then set on top and season.
meal_prep_tip: Not a make-ahead dish — poached eggs and toast are both worse for waiting. It takes five minutes from cold.

name: Post-Workout Recovery Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Drink within 30-60 minutes of training for best effect.
meal_prep_tip: Keep a tub of oats and a pre-measured scoop in your gym bag — this comes together in under a minute post-workout.

name: Prawn & Quinoa Salad
steps: Cook the quinoa according to packet instructions and leave to cool slightly.
Pan-fry the prawns for 2-3 minutes per side until pink and cooked through.
Toss the quinoa with halved cherry tomatoes and diced avocado.
Top with the prawns and a good squeeze of lime.
meal_prep_tip: Best with the prawns cooked fresh, but the quinoa and chopped veg can be prepped up to 3 days ahead.

name: Protein Muffin
steps: Mix all ingredients into a thick batter.
Spoon into a lined muffin tin.
Bake at 180°C for 15-18 minutes until risen and firm to the touch.
Cool before eating; store in the fridge for up to 4 days.
Macros shown are per muffin — the batter makes 2.
meal_prep_tip: Bake a batch and freeze — reheat from frozen in about 30 seconds in the microwave.

name: Protein Pancakes
steps: Blend the oats, protein powder, eggs, banana and cinnamon until smooth.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour small rounds of batter and cook 2 minutes per side until golden.
Stack and serve with fruit or a light drizzle of syrup.
meal_prep_tip: Batch-cook and freeze between sheets of baking paper — reheat straight from frozen in a toaster.

name: Protein Shake & Banana
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink straight away.
meal_prep_tip: Keep pre-portioned bags of frozen banana and a scoop of protein powder ready — this takes under a minute to blend fresh each time.

name: Rice Cakes with Almond Butter
steps: Spread the almond butter over the rice cakes.
Top with banana slices.
Eat immediately for the best crunch.
meal_prep_tip: Quick enough that prepping ahead isn't really necessary, but the almond butter and banana can be portioned into grab-and-go bags.

name: Roasted Chickpeas
steps: Pat the chickpeas dry and toss with oil and spices.
Spread on a tray and roast at 200°C for 25-30 minutes, shaking halfway.
Cool slightly until crisp.
Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.
Macros shown are per serving — this recipe makes 2 servings.
meal_prep_tip: Keeps well in an airtight container for up to a week — a genuinely great batch snack.

name: Salmon Teriyaki with Rice
steps: If time allows, marinate the salmon fillet in 2 tablespoons of the teriyaki sauce for 10-15 minutes at room temperature.
Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Steam or pan-fry the broccoli for 3-4 minutes until bright green and just tender.

Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with a teaspoon of oil. Cook the salmon skin-side down first for 3-4 minutes until the skin is crisp, then flip and cook for another 2-3 minutes. It's done when it flakes at the thickest part but is still slightly translucent in the very centre.
In the final minute, pour the remaining teriyaki sauce into the pan and let it bubble and glaze the salmon.
Serve the salmon over the rice with the broccoli alongside, spooning over any glaze from the pan and scattering with sesame seeds.
meal_prep_tip: Best cooked fresh so the salmon doesn't dry out on reheating, though the rice and broccoli can be prepped ahead.

name: Shakshuka
steps: Sauté the bell pepper until softened, then stir in cumin and harissa.
Add the tinned tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes until thickened.
Make wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook until the whites are set but yolks remain soft; serve straight from the pan.
meal_prep_tip: The tomato base keeps for 4 days or freezes — reheat it and crack in fresh eggs each time rather than pre-cooking them.

name: Skyr with Honey & Nuts
steps: Spoon the skyr into a bowl.
Drizzle with honey.
Top with mixed nuts and serve.
meal_prep_tip: The skyr keeps for the week — just add honey and nuts fresh each time so the nuts stay crunchy.

name: Smoked Haddock Kedgeree
steps: Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then simmer it in 175ml boiling water with the curry powder for 10 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Take off the heat, cover, and rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, lower the egg into boiling water and simmer for 7 minutes for a just-set yolk. Cool under cold running water, then peel.
Poach the haddock in barely simmering water for 4-5 minutes, until it is opaque all the way through and flakes easily with a fork. Drain, then flake into large pieces, discarding any skin and bones.
Stir the frozen peas and butter through the hot rice, cover, and leave for 2 minutes until the peas are bright green and heated through.
Fold the flaked haddock gently through the rice, quarter the egg and set it on top to serve.
meal_prep_tip: Cook the rice and fish a day ahead and chill within an hour of cooking. Reheat once until piping hot and add the egg fresh. Cooked rice should not be kept longer than 24 hours in the fridge.

name: Smoked Salmon Bagel
steps: Slice and toast the bagel.
Spread both halves with the cream cheese alternative.
Layer the smoked salmon and red onion over the base.
Scatter capers on top, close the bagel and serve.
meal_prep_tip: Best assembled fresh so the bagel doesn't go soft, but you can pre-portion the salmon and slice the onion up to 2 days ahead.

name: Smoked Salmon Eggs Benedict
steps: Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer — you want the odd bubble, not a rolling boil, or the whites will shred.
Crack each egg into a cup and slide it in. Poach for 3 minutes for a runny yolk, then lift out with a slotted spoon and rest on kitchen paper.
Split and toast the muffin while the eggs poach. Wilt the spinach in a dry pan for 1 minute and squeeze out any water.
Layer spinach then smoked salmon on each muffin half.
Set a poached egg on each, spoon over the hollandaise and grind on black pepper. Serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Poach the eggs up to a day ahead and drop them into hot water for 45 seconds to reheat. The hollandaise does not keep and should be made fresh.

name: Smoky Chicken Skewers
steps: Cube the chicken into even 2.5cm pieces so they finish cooking at the same time.
Toss with the oil, smoked paprika and a good pinch of salt until evenly coated.
Thread onto two skewers, leaving small gaps between the pieces.
Grill or griddle over a medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until charred outside and white the whole way through.
Squeeze the lemon over while still hot.
meal_prep_tip: Cook a batch and keep them in the fridge for 3 days. Good cold straight from the tub, which is what makes them a snack rather than a meal.

name: Spaghetti Bolognese
steps: Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 4-5 minutes until soft and translucent, then add the minced garlic for the final minute.
Turn the heat up, add the beef mince, and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 5-6 minutes until browned all over with no pink remaining.
Pour in the passata, season with salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar (it balances the acidity), and stir well.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered for at least 20 minutes, stirring occasionally — longer is better if you have time; 45 minutes gives a richer sauce.
About 12 minutes before serving, cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water according to packet instructions until al dente.
Drain the spaghetti, plate it, and spoon the sauce over the top. Add parmesan if you have it. The sauce freezes brilliantly — consider doubling it.
meal_prep_tip: One of the best make-ahead dinners — the sauce keeps for 4 days or freezes for months, and often tastes better the next day.

name: Spiced Carrot & Lentil Soup
steps: Chop the onion and carrot roughly — everything gets blended, so neatness does not matter.
Soften the onion in a dry pan for 5 minutes, then add the cumin and cook for 30 seconds until it smells fragrant.
Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear, then add them with the carrot and stock.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes until the lentils have collapsed and the carrot crushes against the side of the pan.
Blend until smooth, then season. It will thicken as it cools, so loosen with hot water if needed.
meal_prep_tip: The cheapest recipe here by some distance. Makes a double batch easily, keeps 4 days, and freezes for 3 months.

name: Strawberry Banana Milkshake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Pour and serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Use frozen strawberries — equally good and cheaper than fresh, and makes the shake naturally cold.

name: Strawberry Protein Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Pour and serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Frozen strawberries work just as well as fresh and make the shake thicker — keep a bag in the freezer.

name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Tacos
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cube the sweet potato into 2cm chunks, toss with a little oil, salt and smoked paprika if you have it, and roast for 25 minutes until tender and caramelised at the edges.
Warm the black beans in a small pan over low heat with a splash of water and a pinch of cumin, mashing a few lightly so they hold together.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds per side, or wrapped in foil in the oven for the last 5 minutes.
Fill each tortilla with a layer of beans, then the roasted sweet potato.
Top with fresh coriander and a good squeeze of lime — the acidity lifts the whole thing. Eat immediately.
meal_prep_tip: The sweet potato and beans keep for 4 days — just warm the tortillas fresh each time.

name: Thai Green Chicken Soup
steps: Slice the chicken breast into strips about 1cm wide so it cooks quickly and evenly.
Fry the curry paste in a dry pan over a medium heat for 1 minute, until it smells fragrant. This cooks off the raw edge of the spices.
Pour in the stock and coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer, then add the chicken and cook for 8 minutes, until it is white the whole way through with no pink remaining.
Add the mangetout and simmer for a final 2 minutes so they stay crisp and bright green.
Season to taste and serve hot.
meal_prep_tip: Doubles easily. Cool quickly and keep for up to 3 days in the fridge, or a month in the freezer. Add the mangetout when you reheat rather than before freezing, so they stay crisp.

name: Tofu, Greens & Cashew Stir-Fry
steps: Press the tofu between kitchen paper under something heavy for 10 minutes, then cube it. Pressing is what lets it crisp rather than steam.
Cook the noodles to packet instructions, drain, and rinse under cold water so they stop cooking and do not clump.
Get a wok or wide pan very hot. Fry the tofu for 6-8 minutes, turning only when each side has browned, or it will break up.
Add the broccoli and a splash of water, cover for 2 minutes to steam, then uncover and toss until bright green and just tender.
Add the noodles, soy sauce and cashews and toss over a high heat for 1 minute to coat everything.
meal_prep_tip: Doubles well and keeps for 2 days. Cashews soften in the fridge, so hold them back and scatter on after reheating.

name: Trail Mix
steps: Combine all ingredients in a small bowl or bag.
Mix well.
Portion into a container for a grab-and-go snack.
meal_prep_tip: Keeps for weeks in an airtight container — about as batch-friendly as it gets.

name: Tropical Vegan Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Serve immediately, chilled.
meal_prep_tip: Frozen tropical fruit works best here and is often cheaper than fresh — keep a bag ready in the freezer.

name: Tuna & Sweetcorn Pot
steps: Drain the tuna properly, pressing the lid down hard. Watery tuna makes a sloppy pot.
Flake it into a bowl with a fork rather than stirring it to paste.
Fold through the sweetcorn and mayo, keeping some texture.
Season with black pepper and a squeeze of lemon if you have one.
meal_prep_tip: Mix a double batch and keep it covered in the fridge for 2 days. Any longer and the sweetcorn goes soft.

name: Tuna Nicoise Salad
steps: Boil the new potatoes until tender, then set aside to cool slightly.
Blanch the green beans for 2-3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Sear the tuna steak briefly on each side, keeping the centre pink if you like.
Arrange everything with the boiled egg and olives, and dress with olive oil and lemon.
meal_prep_tip: The potatoes, beans and eggs all keep for 3-4 days — sear the tuna fresh, or use tinned tuna for a fully make-ahead version.

name: Tuna Pasta Salad
steps: Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water according to packet instructions (usually 10-12 minutes) until al dente. Drain and rinse under cold water for 30 seconds to stop the cooking and cool it down.
Drain the tin of tuna well and flake it into a large bowl.
Add the sweetcorn and halved cherry tomatoes to the bowl.
Add the cooled pasta and the mayo, and toss until evenly coated. Season with salt, pepper, and a squeeze of lemon if you have one.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate — it keeps well for up to 4 days and is ideal for packed lunches.
meal_prep_tip: A classic make-ahead lunch — keeps well in the fridge for up to 4 days.

name: Turkey & Avocado Wrap
steps: Mash the avocado roughly and spread over the wrap.
Layer the turkey and lettuce on top.
Add a thin line of mustard.
Fold in the sides and roll tightly, then slice in half.
meal_prep_tip: Avocado browns quickly, so mash it fresh each day; the turkey can be sliced and portioned up to 3 days ahead.

name: Turkey & Spinach Breakfast Hash
steps: Dice the sweet potato into 1cm cubes — smaller cubes cook faster and more evenly.

Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the sweet potato and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until the cubes are fork-tender and browning at the edges. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add the turkey mince and diced onion. Break the mince up with a spoon and cook for 5-6 minutes until no pink remains and the onion is soft.
Return the sweet potato to the pan, add the spinach, and stir for 1-2 minutes until the spinach wilts. Season well with salt and pepper.
In a separate small pan, fry or poach the egg to your liking (for a runny yolk, fry over medium heat for about 3 minutes without flipping).
Plate the hash and top with the egg. The runny yolk acts as a sauce.
meal_prep_tip: The hash keeps and reheats well for 3-4 days; fry or poach the egg fresh each time rather than reheating it.

name: Turkey Meatballs with Pasta
steps: Season the turkey mince generously with salt and pepper, then roll into balls about the size of a golf ball — wet hands stop the mixture sticking. You should get 8-10.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the meatballs and brown for 2 minutes per side — they don't need to be cooked through yet.

Pour the tomato sauce over the meatballs, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook for 15 minutes, turning the meatballs halfway. They're done when firm to the touch and no pink remains in the centre (cut one open to check).
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water according to packet instructions until al dente.
Drain the pasta and serve topped with the meatballs and sauce, finished with parmesan and torn basil.
The meatballs and sauce freeze well — cook the pasta fresh when reheating.
meal_prep_tip: The meatballs and sauce keep for 4 days and freeze well — cook the pasta fresh each time for the best texture.

name: Turkey Roll-Ups
steps: Spread a thin layer of the cream cheese alternative over each turkey slice.
Lay a cucumber strip along one edge.
Roll up tightly.
Repeat and serve chilled.
meal_prep_tip: Best rolled fresh so the cucumber stays crisp, but the turkey and cream cheese can be portioned ahead.

name: Tzatziki & Pitta
steps: Coarsely grate the cucumber, then squeeze it hard in a clean tea towel. This is the step people skip and it is why tzatziki turns watery.
Crush the garlic to a paste with a pinch of salt.
Stir the cucumber and garlic through the yogurt and season. Rest for 10 minutes so the garlic mellows.
Toast the pitta until puffed, then tear or cut into strips for dipping.
meal_prep_tip: The tzatziki keeps for 3 days and improves overnight. Toast the pitta fresh — it goes leathery once cooled.

name: Vegan Berry Protein Shake
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Serve immediately while cold.
meal_prep_tip: Freeze pre-portioned bags of berries and spinach — just add protein powder and oat milk and blend straight from frozen.

name: Vegan Black Bean Chilli
steps: Simmer the beans with the tinned tomato and chilli for 20 minutes, mashing some beans to thicken.
Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Season the chilli to taste.
Serve the chilli over the rice.
meal_prep_tip: Freezes well and keeps in the fridge for 4-5 days — a great batch-cook option.

name: Vegan Chickpea Buddha Bowl
steps: Roast the sweet potato cubes at 200°C for 25 minutes until tender.
Cook the quinoa according to packet instructions.
Massage the kale briefly with a little oil to soften it.
Assemble the bowl and finish with a tahini drizzle, thinned with a splash of water if needed.
meal_prep_tip: Roast a big tray of sweet potato and cook a batch of quinoa on Sunday — assembles in 2 minutes for the rest of the week.

name: Vegan Mushroom Risotto
steps: Sauté the mushrooms until golden, then set aside.
Toast the rice briefly in the same pan, then add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring until absorbed before adding more.
Continue for about 18-20 minutes until the rice is creamy and just tender.
Stir through the mushrooms, nutritional yeast and thyme before serving.
meal_prep_tip: Best fresh — it firms up and loses its creaminess once cold — though the mushrooms and stock can be prepped ahead.

name: Vegan Protein Balls
steps: Blitz the dates in a food processor until they form a paste.
Add the remaining ingredients and pulse until a sticky dough forms.
Roll into 8-10 balls.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before eating; store in the fridge.
Macros shown are per 2 balls — the batch makes 8-10.
meal_prep_tip: Keeps in the fridge for a week or freezes for months — one of the best batch-prep snacks here.

name: Vegan Protein Pasta Salad
steps: Cook the chickpea pasta according to packet instructions, then cool under cold water.
Whisk the protein powder into a little water or the olive oil to form a light dressing.
Toss the pasta with halved cherry tomatoes and torn basil.
Stir through the dressing just before serving.
meal_prep_tip: Keeps well cold for 3-4 days — a genuine make-ahead lunch.

name: Vegan Protein Smoothie Bowl
steps: Blend the frozen banana, protein powder, oat milk and spinach until thick and smooth.
Pour into a bowl.
Top with granola and any extra fruit you like.
Eat immediately with a spoon while thick.
meal_prep_tip: Best blended fresh for texture, but you can freeze pre-portioned bags of banana and spinach so you just add liquid and blend.

name: Vegan Protein Stir Fry
steps: Cook the brown rice according to packet instructions — brown rice typically takes 25-30 minutes, so start it first.
Press the tofu between kitchen paper with a weight on top for 10 minutes to remove excess moisture, then cut into 2cm cubes.

Heat a tablespoon of oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat. Add the tofu cubes and fry for 6-8 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until golden and crisp on most sides. Remove and set aside.
Add the mixed vegetables to the hot pan and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until just tender but still with bite.
Return the tofu to the pan and add the soy sauce, tossing to coat.
Whisk the protein powder into 3 tablespoons of cold water until smooth, pour it in, and stir for 30 seconds — it will thicken into a light glaze. Serve immediately over the rice.
meal_prep_tip: Like most stir-fries, best cooked fresh for texture — the tofu can be pressed and cubed ahead of time.

name: Vegan Tofu Scramble
steps: Press the tofu briefly, then crumble it into a hot, lightly oiled pan.
Stir in the turmeric and cook for 3-4 minutes until it looks scrambled.
Add the spinach and halved cherry tomatoes, cooking until the spinach wilts.
Stir through the nutritional yeast, season, and serve.
meal_prep_tip: Cooks and reheats well — make a big batch and portion into containers for 3-4 days.

name: Veggie Omelette
steps: Crack 3 eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and pepper, and whisk with a fork for 20-30 seconds until fully blended with no streaks of white.

Heat a small non-stick frying pan (about 20cm) over medium heat with a teaspoon of oil or butter. Add the sliced mushroom and diced red pepper and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms have softened and released their moisture.
Add the spinach and stir for 30-60 seconds until just wilted.
Pour the whisked eggs over the vegetables, tilting the pan so they spread evenly. Cook undisturbed for about 1 minute until the edges start to set.

Sprinkle the grated cheddar over one half. Using a spatula, gently lift the edges and tilt the pan so uncooked egg runs underneath. When the surface is mostly set but still slightly glossy (about 2-3 minutes total), fold the omelette in half over the cheese.
Cook for a further 30-60 seconds, then slide onto a plate and serve immediately.
meal_prep_tip: Omelettes are best fresh, but you can pre-chop all the veg and grate the cheese up to 3 days ahead.
